overall_summary: Space anomalies and extreme natural phenomena are currently driving the highest engagement and views on the channel, led by 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,053 views) and 'The Largest Ocean in Space' (460 views). Conversely, cognitive psychology and brain-related facts are underperforming, with multiple uploads failing to cross the 100-view threshold. Sensory-driven hooks that challenge physical intuition (e.g., smells, extreme temperatures, physical states) significantly outperform abstract concepts.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Space Anomalies with Sensory Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' reached 1,053 views and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' reached 368 views, showing a strong response to tactile, visceral cosmic concepts.
winning_patterns.action: Prioritize space topics that contrast opposing physical states (e.g., hot/cold, liquid/gas) or introduce unexpected sensory details.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees' (302 views) and 'This Animal Literally Dies Every Winter!' (179 views) outperformed standard anatomical trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Focus animal content on extreme survival mechanisms, evolutionary paradoxes, and high-stakes biological feats.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (54 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) struggled to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid generic self-help or common psychological observations; pivot psychology content toward high-stakes historical mysteries or bizarre clinical syndromes.
